newsitem.title: USA: WorldCom now in play -- takeover specialist.
newsitem.headline: WorldCom now in play -- takeover specialist.

text.p: Regional Bells across the U.S. will now be running their spreadsheets over WorldCom Inc, knowing this is their last chance to buy it, according to a mergers and acquisition specialist.

Robert McNamara of takeover consultancy Broadview Associates said that WorldCom, a long-rumored bid target, has effectively put itself in play with its brilliant but earnings -dilutive takeover of MFS Communications Co Inc .
"You have effectively put WorldCom into play with this move," McNamara said on Monday.
He said that WorldCom and MFS were aware of this and had put in a $350 million break-up fee and 20 percent lock-up options into the final agreement to forestall a bid.
WorldCom has for years been considered by analysts a juicy target for any regional Bell that had ambitions to own a long distance and international network.
The story has cooled in recent years as the market value of WorldCom mushroomed. WorldCom stock closed 3-5/8 down, or 14 percent, at 22-3/4, capitalising the firm at $9.5 billion.
But McNamara said that all the hurdles could be overcome at a price, and weakness of WorldCom stock because of the MFS takeover might provide the opportunity.
"I don't believe there is a regional Bell out there that couldn't pay it. A 30 percent premium over today's price would be enough to get shareholders' interests," he said.
The break-up fee would be payable by whichever party failed to complete the MFS transaction -- WorldCom in the case that it was bought by an outside bidder.
The lock-up options give either company the right to buy stock in the other at prices above current prices.
WorldCom also on Monday adopted a shareholder rights plan that would allow for a dividend distribution of preferred shares triggered by a hostile stake of 15 percent or more.
